question: A 32-year-old Caucasian female is admitted to the emergency department with a 48-hour history of severe and diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation. Her personal history is unremarkable except for an ectopic pregnancy 5 years ago. Upon admission, she is found to have a blood pressure of 120/60 mm Hg, a pulse of 105/min, a respiratory rate 20/min, and a body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F). She has diffuse abdominal tenderness, hypoactive bowel sounds, and mild distention on examination of her abdomen. Rectal and pelvic examination findings are normal. An abdominal plain film of the patient is given. What is the most likely cause of this patient’s condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Severe and diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation" -> "Diffuse abdominal tenderness, hypoactive bowel sounds, and mild distention" -> "Abdominal plain film findings" -> 70% CHAIN: "Ectopic pregnancy history" -> "Possible adhesions formation" -> "Abdominal symptoms presentation" -> 60% CHAIN: "Normal rectal and pelvic examination findings" -> "Less likely gastrointestinal malignancy" -> "Abdominal plain film findings" -> 80% CHAIN: "Blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg, pulse 105/min, respiratory rate 20/min, body temperature 37°C" -> "Hemodynamically stable" -> "Less likely malrotation requiring urgent intervention" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely cause of this patient's condition is adhesions. The presentation of severe and diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation along with a history of ectopic pregnancy suggests possible adhesions formation. The absence of abnormal findings on rectal and pelvic examination makes gastrointestinal malignancy less likely. The patient's stable hemodynamics also make malrotation less probable. The abdominal plain film findings may further support the presence of adhesions.
